Barkpark Connectors — Wave 1 (P0): the tenant seam + the engine seam

Status: BUILDING (Decide complete). This Paper is the living spine of Connectors Wave 1. It opens here with the wish, the strategic direction, and the survey plan; Digest will append the survey findings + the verify fleet; Decide will append the ratified slice plan; Review closes it as the debrief. Someone opening this mid-wave sees exactly where the wave stands.

Epic task: 00035edc-59f4-4775-ba76-246eb14914bf — "Barkpark Connectors — integrate agents with external services". Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-connectors-charter.md. Design paper: /papers/personal-agent-provider-bridge. This epic is a deliberate semantic near-twin of viable-everywhere-epic and is filed distinct_from:["viable-everywhere-epic"] — viable-everywhere makes the Barkpark server reachable remotely (MCP-OAuth); Connectors makes agents talk through chat services with the Session as memory. Different seam, different product.

The wish (verbatim intent)

Connect Barkpark with Slack or Discord so Barkpark Chat acts as a Personal Agent, using the Session to contain memory, connected conveniently — and more broadly, make it VERY EASY to integrate Barkpark agents with services like these. First-focus channels, all at once: Slack, Discord, Telegram, Teams, WhatsApp, iMessage. Cloud multi-tenant from day one. Scope THIS wave to P0 ONLY per the charter.

The finished experience we are building toward

A workspace connects its agent to the services its people already live in. You DM the agent on Slack Monday, continue the same thread on Discord Friday, and it remembers — because a Barkpark Session is the memory, reachable from any channel. Connecting is a two-minute product action (Studio → Connectors → +Slack → OAuth → pick an agent → done), not an integration project. Every workspace runs its own connectors, credentials isolated, the Cloud tenant's agent sandboxed with no host access. The Kinsta/Vercel bar is the connect flow feeling like a first-class product surface — but that flow (P2/P3) rides on two foundations that do not exist yet on main. This wave builds ONLY those two foundations, and builds them so the bridge drops onto them cleanly later.

What Wave 1 is — and is not

P0 = the tenant seam + the engine seam. Runner-independent, no channel code, no Chat SDK yet. Two verify legs gate two build slices; one long-lead human gate runs in parallel. We do NOT touch P1 (the sandboxed runner) because D10 is an open fork — that decision must be resolved with cold-start numbers in a later wave, not guessed at now.

Confirmed on main during Strategize (pre-survey reconnaissance)

  • D7 leak shape CONFIRMED. api/lib/barkpark/studio_chat/session.ex — the chat_sessions schema has NO owner/workspace column. Primary key is the minted claude session UUID (autogenerate: false); every field is conversation state (title, cwd, mode, tokens, rail_snapshot). It is instance-global, admin-gated. There are ~10 additive migrations under api/priv/repo/migrations/*chat_sessions*, none of them scoping. This is exactly the leak: any admin sees every tenant's sessions.
  • D8 status CONFIRMED. grep -rn "v1/chat" api/lib/ returns NOTHING. router.ex carries only LiveView /chat + /chat/:session_id (Studio, admin-gated). The HTTP+SSE transport is not on main — it lives in the chat-tui epic's worktrees/branches (memory: "SSE transport chosen, MVP build resumed"). There is an active worktree omx/task151-chat-charter and the chat-tui epic is a hot concurrent-dev area — coordination risk is real.
  • Adjacent primitives exist and P0 must ride them, not rebuild: encrypted run-secrets (deployed on guerrilla — secrets.ex, workspace-scoping granularity TBD by survey), the user-principal seam from airdrop grants (merged #1276), the tenancy contract (scoped reads filter dataset_id with NO NULL-fallback), and the StudioChat claude-subprocess spawn model (session UUID minted before first byte, same value is --resume).

Strategic direction (tentative — Decide finalizes after two explore rounds)

  1. The proof is the product this wave. Wave 1 succeeds when we can, via curl: create a workspace-owned session, POST a message, read the streamed SSE reply — AND a second tenant provably CANNOT see or resume it. That cross-tenant LEAK negative test is not optional; without it a green pass is meaningless (sessions/tenancy are maximum blast radius).
  2. Slice A — the tenant seam (D7 build). Add owner_workspace_id to chat_sessions + a principal for the external user, riding the merged user-principal seam and the tenancy contract. Migration is additive/nullable (pre-migration rows read "unowned, admin-only"). All read/list/resume paths in StudioChat get scoped and fail closed. I lean toward: reuse the airdrop-grants principal shape verbatim rather than invent a new external-user identity.
  3. Slice B — the engine seam (D8 build). Land/confirm /v1/chat HTTP+SSE on main: create session, POST message, read SSE reply. I lean toward: adopt (rebase/cherry-pick) the chat-tui epic's already-chosen wire contract rather than fork a second one — the survey must find that contract and tell us if it is landable clean or entangled. The wire contract for /v1/chat and the thread_id → session_uuid map is FIXED in the charter; parallel builders share that one written truth. SSE should reuse the existing /v1/data/listen streaming pattern, not invent a new transport.
  4. Design for the bridge we are not building yet. P2's Chat SDK bridge holds only thread_id → session_uuid as per-conversation state. Slice B's transport and Slice A's ownership must be shaped so that map drops on cleanly — the external principal on the session IS the future Slack-user identity. Do not paint P2 into a corner.
  5. Teams Azure Bot registration — parallel long-lead human gate. File now so it runs alongside P0; it blocks nothing in the build (fakes first), gates only go-live of the heavy pair much later. Same pattern as the GitHub-App and Vercel-token human gates.
  6. Hold the line on D10. No runner work. If a slice starts reaching for sandbox shape, it has drifted out of P0.

Where the quality bar is NOT yet met

Nowhere in P0 is a user-facing surface — that is intentional. The risk this wave is structural: shipping a tenant seam that leaks, an SSE transport that duplicates rather than reuses, or an ownership model the P2 bridge cannot map onto. The bar this wave is correctness-under-adversarial-test and clean-seam-for-later, not polish.

Survey plan (the wide net — every question + why)

16 broad Sonnet surveyors. Width is cheap now; Digest distills. Each names suspected files, prior art (repo AND bp papers/tasks), or a seam to map.

  • chat-sessions-schema — Full column/migration truth of chat_sessions: any latent scoping, the admin gate, indexes. Why: exact starting shape for the D7 migration.
  • session-read-paths — Every place StudioChat reads/lists/resumes a session (studio_chat.ex, ChatLive, any controller). Which would leak cross-tenant after ownership lands? Why: the leak negative-test target set + the seal-each-bypass work.
  • v1-chat-location — WHERE the /v1/chat HTTP+SSE transport actually lives (chat-tui branches/worktrees), how complete, its exact wire contract (create/POST/SSE frame shape). Why: Slice B is land-or-fork; this decides which.
  • chat-tui-epic-state — The chat-tui epic's state, tasks, and whether its /v1/chat work is mergeable or entangled with TUI-only code. Concurrent-dev collision risk. Why: coordination + landability of Slice B.
  • user-principal-seam — How airdrop-grants principals work (merged #1276): principal shape, external-user identity, how a non-account actor maps to a workspace. Why: Slice A's external principal rides this — reuse vs invent.
  • tenancy-contract — docs/contracts/tenancy.md + enforcement: workspace/project/dataset scoping, the NULL-scope-invisible rule, how owner columns are enforced elsewhere. Why: how owner_workspace_id should filter + fail closed.
  • run-secrets-scoping — Is the deployed run-secrets store workspace-scoped, and at what granularity? secrets.ex, secret_record.ex. Why: D9 later needs per-workspace bot tokens; confirm the shape now so P0's seam aligns.
  • subprocess-spawn-model — How StudioChat spawns the claude CLI: port/System.cmd, --session-id/--resume, cwd, permission mode, host access. Why: constrains what a Cloud runner replaces (D5) and how /v1/chat drives a turn.
  • design-paper-contract — Full read of /papers/personal-agent-provider-bridge: every architectural commitment, the wire contract + thread→session map details, anything the charter compressed. Why: the authoritative spec; catch drift.
  • sse-patterns — How /v1/data/listen/:dataset streams SSE (auth on SSE, keepalive, framing, Phoenix mechanism). Why: Slice B should reuse this, not invent a transport.
  • viable-everywhere-dedup — What viable-everywhere-epic actually built (MCP-OAuth, remote reachability); the precise dedup boundary; any seam (auth/principal/remote transport) Connectors should reuse. Why: confirm distinct_from is honest + harvest reuse.
  • connectors-epic-tree — Existing child tasks under the Connectors epic; any prior/partial work; wave_status/wave_paper fields. Why: don't refile what exists; find partial slices.
  • vercel-chat-sdk — What the chat npm package (Vercel Chat SDK) provides: adapter model, thread.stream(), webhook shape, per-tenant routing hooks. Why: shapes P0's transport so the P2 bridge is a thin client.
  • teams-azure-longlead — What Teams Azure Bot / Bot Framework registration actually requires (AAD app, Bot channel reg, credentials, human steps). Why: author the parallel long-lead human-gated task precisely.
  • worktree-elixir-gate — The lockfree-worktree-gate + migrate-before-seed recipe for Elixir migration builds (cp _build/test, symlink deps, never symlink _build, ecto.migrate before seeding a new table). Why: both slices touch .ex/migrations; builders must isolate correctly.
  • mcp-serve-mirror — bp mcp serve and the tool-connector mirror (agent consuming an external MCP). Why: the other arrow of the catalog; confirm P0's seam doesn't foreclose the tool direction.

Digest — survey folded, verify fleet designed (Fable/Opus)

16 Sonnet surveyors returned. This section folds their evidence into decisions-in-waiting and launches the LAST explore round — 6 targeted verifiers. After this round the plan is cut. All phases pinned to Opus this run (Fable out of credits); every build slice will be builder_model:opus, never fable.

The headline overturns the Strategize premise: D8 is already DONE

The single most consequential finding: the /v1/chat HTTP+SSE transport is not missing from main — it was merged and is live. PR #2857 (commit 0b699edf, merged 2026-07-13) landed the full 8-route controller + SSE; git merge-base --is-ancestor 0b699edf origin/main returns true, and curl https://guerrilla.barkpark.cloud/v1/chat/sessions returns 401, not 404 — the route exists and is auth-gated, auto-deployed on merge. The pre-survey D8 recon ("grep v1/chat returns nothing") was run against the LOCAL checkout, which is 59 commits behind / 108 diverged from origin/main and simply never received the chat-tui epic's merge.

Contradiction reconciled: two surveyors (sse-patterns, design-paper-contract) reported the transport "lives only in worktrees, not on main" — but they grepped the stale local tree / a worktree. Two others (v1-chat-location, chat-tui-epic-state) PROVED the merge with is-ancestor against origin/main + a live curl. Resolution: the transport is on origin/main AND replicated across many worktrees (pre-merge dev branches + concurrent wave-2 forks). Trust the git-proven finding.

Consequence for Slice B: it collapses from "land/confirm the transport" to "pull origin/main; the transport is already there." Crucially, the wave's proof-is-the-product cross-tenant negative test CANNOT be written against today's transport — there is no tenant boundary yet (all routes are [:api, :require_admin], instance-global). It becomes writable only AFTER Slice A adds owner_workspace_id. Slice A gates the wave's proof, not Slice B.

The leak now has TWO surfaces — Slice A must seal both

The merged ChatController's own read/list/resume/mutate paths key purely on session_id (same leak shape as StudioChat), and its routes are hardcoded :require_admin with no tenancy. So once multi-tenant, the leak is reachable through both the LiveView (StudioChat + chat_live.ex) AND the HTTP controller. Slice A must (a) add the column, (b) seal every read/list/resume path on both surfaces to fail closed, and (c) re-gate the /v1/chat routes from :require_admin to workspace-scoped auth. Slice A and Slice B are coupled at exactly that auth-pipeline seam — not independent.

D7 confirmed overwhelmingly — the leak is total, not partial

Six surveyors independently confirmed chat_sessions has ZERO owner/workspace/tenant column across the base + 8 additive migrations; PK is the minted claude UUID (autogenerate: false). get_session/1 is a bare Repo.get by UUID. Seal surface: 6 StudioChat funnel functions (get/get_with_messages/list_sessions/list_messages/delete/archive-unarchive) + 5 chat_live.ex call sites (handle_params:312 resume; handle_event archive/delete:842-857 — MUTATE paths; refresh_sessions:3885; re-fetch:4216) + the merged controller's 8 routes. The mutate paths matter: a wrong-tenant attacker could delete another tenant's session even if reads are sealed — the negative test must cover mutation, not just reads.

The principal-shape fork — the direction's "ride airdrop-grants verbatim" is the wrong precedent for the external user

Slice A's largest design decision. The airdrop-grants Grant shape does not fit a Slack/Discord end-user: a Grant only becomes live via ClaimFlow.resolve/2, which requires an authenticated, email-matching, confirmed_at-set Accounts.User (claim_flow.ex:53-64). A chat-service user has no Barkpark account. What is reusable is the scope-ladder + live-re-validation pattern (Access.scope_contained?, grantor_authorizes?), not the Grant schema. The closer structural analog is Auth.ApiToken (workspace_id + extensible kind, e.g. the "ticket" precedent, + optional owner_user_id). CallerContext.principal_type is a closed 3-value enum (:anonymous | :api_token | :user) — the natural extension point. Three candidate shapes for Decide: (a) new ApiToken kind:"chat_bridge"; (b) new CallerContext principal_type + an external_identities table keyed (provider, external_user_id) → workspace; (c) a chat_sessions-scoped narrow principal. This fork goes to a verifier.

The NULL-fallback fork — copy scope_to_workspace, NOT scope_to_owner

owner_workspace_id is a tenant-boundary column, so it must follow scope_to_workspace/3 (nil → where(false), zero rows) — NOT scope_to_owner's "OR owner_id IS NULL" carve-out (per-user ownership; would leave legacy rows visible workspace-wide = a leak), and NOT dataset scoping's legacy string OR-fallback (a NULL-visible hole). Pre-migration NULL rows should read admin-only / invisible-to-tenants (zero rows under scope_to_workspace). Additive-nullable-no-FK-indexed precedent: 20260629150300_add_owner_id_to_documents.exs. Note a likely new composite index [:owner_workspace_id, :last_active_at] for the per-tenant sidebar query (existing indexes don't help a scoped read).

D9 run-secrets — the charter premise is WRONG (P1, not this wave)

secrets is a FLAT instance-global name→value KV (PK = bare name, no workspace_id; list/0 returns every secret masked with no tenant filter; gated by the flat :require_admin, not :scoped_admin). The sibling plugin_settings KV is identically unscoped — this is BP Cloud's established KV shape. The charter's D9 ("confirm scoping granularity") assumes workspace-scoped; granularity is NONE. Real per-workspace bot tokens need a schema migration + scoped-admin gate — a build, analogous to Slice A. This is out of P0 scope, but Decide must NOT inherit the false "already deployed, just confirm" assumption. File as backlog + correct charter D9.

Settled by survey — no re-verification (evidence was strong)

  • Worktree Elixir gate — recipe confirmed 3× (connectors charter :57, cloud-build D16, lockfree-worktree-gate memory): COPY _build/test (never symlink — symlinking trips the :media_upload_dir @compile_env boot-abort on __DIR__ mismatch), symlink deps, CC=clang, mix ecto.migrate before seeding a new table. Proven green on a migration+new-module diff — exactly Slice A's shape.
  • SSE reuse — the merged ChatController.events already reuses the ListenController pattern near-verbatim (max_heap_size guard, spawn_link forwarder, Last-Event-ID replay, 30s keepalive). Deliberate divergence: chat has NO backpressure shed (charter D5 "never shed-and-close"). Slice B does not invent a transport.
  • Subprocess spawn — Port.open via /bin/sh -c exec, --session-id/--resume mutually exclusive, cwd = server's own File.cwd!() (no per-tenant sandbox — that's D5/P1), env scrub-list, Recorder is the permanent PubSub sink on studio_chat:<id>.
  • MCP mirror — P0 does not foreclose the tool direction; only a loopback MCP-client exists today; P4 outbound is unbuilt.
  • Vercel Chat SDK — not vendored anywhere (P2 greenfield); per-tenant routing is Barkpark's job (D9), not SDK-provided.
  • viable-everywhere dedup — HONEST. It built stateless MCP-OAuth reachability (Go-side, deployed); its OAuth-AS is an unbuilt placeholder. No session/tenancy code to collide. The reusable seam (CallerContext + Tenancy.Auth) comes from airdrop-grants, not viable-everywhere. File distinct_from as-is (note: it is prose-only, not a structured field).
  • Teams — domain-knowledge recipe (AAD app + multi-tenant Azure Bot + Teams channel + manifest + org consent). Model the task on the GitHub-App human-gate doc (docs/ops/github-sync.md): runbook + secrets table + verify round-trip + "blocks no code" framing. File parallel long-lead.

Coverage map — checked & FOUND vs checked & NOT-FOUND (absences are decisions-in-waiting)

Found & proven: chat_sessions schema (full column truth, 6 surveyors); the unscoped StudioChat + chat_live seal surface; the /v1/chat transport merged+live on origin/main; the ChatController wire contract + SSE frame shapes; scope.ex's three distinct fail-closed mechanisms; ApiToken/CallerContext/Tenancy.Auth principal machinery; the worktree gate recipe; the epic task (zero children, wave fields set).

Checked & NOT found (each a decision-in-waiting):

  • NO owner/workspace/tenant column on chat_sessions or chat_messages — total absence, all migrations read. Slice A designs it from scratch.
  • NO existing external_user/external_principal/service_account/bot_user concept anywhere in api/lib — Slice A must DESIGN the external principal, not wire one up.
  • NO /v1/chat on the LOCAL checkout (stale) — but PRESENT on origin/main.
  • NO Vercel Chat SDK (chat npm / @chat-adapter/*) vendored — P2 greenfield.
  • NO production outbound MCP-client code — P4 unbuilt.
  • NO workspace scoping on secrets — flat KV (D9 false premise).

Corners no surveyor conclusively reached (routed to verify or left for build): whether chat_messages needs its own tenant column or session-join scoping suffices; whether an existing test file can be extended into the cross-tenant negative test; whether concurrent chat-tui wave-2 PRs will land on session.ex/chat_controller.ex mid-wave; the exact freshest worktree (moot now that the transport is on main). Also: bp search does not exist in this CLI build — every surveyor hit the usage error; the "bp search first" doctrine is stale for this binary (search is an HTTP verb only).

Ledger correction found: the epic task's real doc id is task-e640bb01fca6ea38 (content.id 22076fb0-…); this Paper's Strategize text cites 00035edc-59f4-4775-…, which does NOT resolve. Decide fixes the reference and files children under the correct id.

Not sent to verify (settled or out of P0): worktree gate recipe, SSE reuse pattern, subprocess model, MCP mirror, Vercel SDK absence, D9 run-secrets shape (all confirmed by survey with strong evidence; D9 is a P1 backlog correction, not a P0 gate).

DECIDE — 2026-07-13 (two verify rounds in hand; builders fly next)

Status: DECIDING → BUILDING. The verify fleet settled every open leg. The headline: the D8 transport we planned to "land" is already merged and live. The wave is three parallel-file slices, all builder_model: opus (Fable is out of credits this run).

Verification results — what was proven (proofs > prose)

  • V1 — transport ALREADY ON MAIN. git merge-base --is-ancestor 0b699edf origin/main → TRANSPORT_ON_MAIN; PR #2857 merged an 8-route ChatController (CRUD + send/interrupt/approval + SSE, 39 tests) on 2026-07-13; guerrilla /v1/chat/sessions answers 401, not 404. The local primary checkout is a diverged fork ~109 commits behind and never received the merge — that is why the pre-survey grep found nothing. Consequence: Slice B is "tenant-scope the existing one," and every builder branches off origin/main.
  • V1/V4 — D7 leak is TOTAL and greenfield. git show origin/main:.../studio_chat/session.ex | grep -in 'owner|workspace|tenant' → NO_TENANT_COLUMN. No prior scoping migration exists; the migration is additive/greenfield.
  • V2 — the seal belongs at the STORE layer. chat_live.ex bypasses the controller and calls StudioChat funnels directly (get_session@318/@4256, list_sessions@3925, delete@861, archive@849); sealing only the controller leaves the LiveView sidebar open. require_admin checks a flat global permission with no workspace param and the routes carry no /w/:ws segment → a pipeline swap is breaking, not additive. No open PR collides on the four seal files.
  • V3 — airdrop Grant/ClaimFlow is the WRONG principal. ClaimFlow.resolve/2 requires an authenticated, email-matching, confirmed_at-set User — an account-less Slack/Discord identity can never pass. ApiToken already is a workspace-bound principal with an extensible kind and a nullable owner_user_id; Tickets' kind:"ticket" is live precedent for a token tier without touching the isolation core.
  • V4 — scope rule settled. scope_to_workspace(query, nil, _) → where(query, false) (fail-closed, zero rows). Do NOT use scope_to_owner's OR is_nil(owner_id) carve-out (blanket-exposes legacy rows) nor the dataset OR string shim. Composite partial index [owner_workspace_id, last_active_at] WHERE archived_at IS NULL mirrors the existing sidebar index idiom.
  • V5 — negative-test seam is hybrid. chat_controller_test.exs already has a passing test asserting the leak ("two distinct global-admin tokens both read the SAME session") — invert it; Auth.create_token/5 already takes an optional workspace_id. Store-layer delete/archive/unarchive have NO caller argument today → their signatures must change before any tenant test can exercise them.
  • V6 — ledger clean. Epic task-e640bb01fca6ea38 had zero children; the Paper's cited UUID 00035edc-… does not resolve (a paste slip — corrected below); no duplicate Teams task exists.

Coverage / not-founds: V6 confirmed no Teams/Azure-Bot duplicate task via full-text search (only stemmed false positives). V3 did not open the charter this pass but the code evidence makes ApiToken the lean pick regardless. V2 did not exhaustively line-trace every mutate helper in chat_live (all key on session_id via get_session, so they inherit the store seal). The Recorder/PubSub SSE subscription is not tenant-aware — Slice B must scope get_session before subscribing.

Decisions (D13–D20 — mirror the charter)

  • D13 — Transport is already merged. Slice B tenant-scopes the merged /v1/chat; all builders branch off origin/main. Why: local checkout lacks the ChatController entirely.
  • D14 — Migration additive/greenfield. owner_workspace_id :binary_id null:true, no FK/default; legacy NULL rows read admin/:global-only. Why: zero prior column, mirror the documents owner_id rollout.
  • D15 — scope_to_workspace semantics only. Fail-closed equality; no OR-is_nil, no dataset OR-fallback; add the partial composite index. Why: either carve-out re-opens the leak by making unscoped rows blanket-visible.
  • D16 — Principal = ApiToken (chat permission), NOT airdrop Grant. No new principal_type/CallerContext/Membership edits. Why: account-less chat identity can't pass ClaimFlow; ApiToken already carries workspace_id.
  • D17 — Seal at the STORE layer. Funnels take scope (:global | workspace_id); both controller and chat_live pass through the sealed funnels. Why: chat_live bypasses the controller.
  • D18 — Additive auth, not a breaking swap. New RequireChatAccess plug: global-admin → :global (unchanged), workspace token with chat perm → {:workspace, ws}. Why: require_admin is flat-global; keep live admin usage working.
  • D19 — Cross-tenant negative test mandatory + hybrid. Controller 404-oracle across 8 routes + store/LiveView fail-closed + events scope-before-subscribe. Why: sessions/tenancy = max blast radius; distrust vacuous green.
  • D20 — Hold the line on D10. No runner/sandbox work this wave. Why: the fork needs cold-start numbers first.

Also corrected this Decide: the Paper's epic reference is task-e640bb01fca6ea38 (content id 22076fb0-…), not the dangling 00035edc-…. D9's "run-secrets is workspace-scoped" premise is FALSE (flat instance-global KV) — filed as a P1 backlog correction, not a P0 gate.

The cross-slice bug the review caught (and fixed)

The two slices took different enforcement models: Slice A stamps ownership at the store from a scope arg (authoritative — it OVERRIDES any owner_workspace_id in attrs), while Slice B (built against origin/main without A present) smuggled the owner through attrs and enforced with a controller-level visible?/2 reading Map.get(session, :owner_workspace_id). On the merged state these collided: the controller called create_session/1 with the owner in attrs but no scope arg, so A's store defaulted the scope to :global and nulled the owner. Net effect: a workspace connector created a nil-owned session and then 404'd on its own session — the exact WISH-critical path (a tenant talking to its agent through a session it owns) was broken, while the builders' green tests never exercised the positive "owner reads back its own session" leg (partially-vacuous on precisely the leg that matters).

Fix (commit on slice-b-...-1-r): the controller now threads scope(conn) into create_session/2 so the store stamps the owner; index uses the DB-scoped list_sessions/2 (charter D15 partial index) instead of an after-the-fact in-memory filter that a busy instance could starve past @sidebar_cap; fetch_scoped reads through the sealed store get_session/2 (charter D17 single enforcement point); the now-dead controller-level visible?/2 and owner_for/1 were removed. A protective test was added — ws-A creates a session and reads it back (200) and lists it, ws-B is 404'd on that fresh id. This leg FAILS under the nil-owner bug and PASSES after the fix (verified: seen red, then green).

Ledger audit outcome

  • False-done corrected (Slice A + Slice B): both slice tasks carried an off-by-one criterion stamp — criterion [0] (the delivered migration/plug) was left unmet with empty evidence, while criterion [4] ("PR merged — LEAD closes") was FALSELY marked met=True. Builders must never close a merge-gated criterion. The reviewer un-shifted the evidence to its correct criteria, flipped [0..3] to met, and reset [4] to met=False (awaiting LEAD merge). Slice C was already stamped correctly.
  • Epic distinct_from added: the WISH explicitly required distinct_from:["viable-everywhere-epic"] on the epic task; it was missing and has been patched in.
  • All three built slices left lifecycle in_progress (correct — the LEAD closes on merge). The three backlog tasks (P1 run-secrets, P1 sandbox runner, P2 bridge) are correctly open and were not touched. No task outside this wave was modified.

Grade — A−

Excellent scoped delivery. The wave nails exactly the P0 seam the charter asked for: a fail-closed tenant column on chat_sessions, a scoped transport that fails to the not-found oracle, and a long-lead Teams runbook filed in parallel — with P1/P2 correctly deferred and filed as backlog. The store seal is careful and charter-faithful; the Teams doc is genuinely production-grade. What holds it back from an A: a real merged-state isolation bug slipped through the builders' green because their tests were vacuous on the one positive leg the WISH is about (owner reads its own session), and the ledger carried a false-done on the merge criterion. Both were caught and fixed before merge, and the merged artifact is now correct, isolated, and gate-green — hence a strong A−, not lower.

What the next wave should take

P0 is done once the LEAD merges A then B-r (B-r already contains A via rebase; merge A first, then B-r, behind the Elixir Test gate — the merge-gated criterion [4] on both tasks is the LEAD's to close). The next wave is P1: resolve the D10 open fork with a real ≤10s cold-start benchmark for the sandbox runner (task-6672a70bea19dc11) and scope run-secrets per-workspace (task-5766dc5ca985ddc8, the D9 premise correction — run-secrets is currently flat instance-global, which the Teams runbook's "workspace-scoped secrets" assumes lands here). Do NOT start P2 (Chat SDK bridge, task-6c358e166b6c7eaf) until P0 has merged. One carry-forward note for P1/P2: the chat permission string is not in any registry — if a permission allowlist is ever enforced, register it.
